title: Last Bell, 2016
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · the aggregator
logline: The bell. Gully's girl finishes kindergarten. Wood frames her drawing of a crab. Red frame.

panels.composition: Gully's. GULLY's girl, six, with a crayon drawing: a crab, twelve legs. GULLY. WOOD on the stool. The bell, faint, from the school.

image.prompt: a six-year-old girl holding up a crayon drawing of a twelve-legged crab at a bait-shop counter, a man in an apron, a thin man on a stool, a three-legged dog, a faint distant bell

panels.composition: Wood looking at the drawing. The 2000 frame-shop father's kid's drawing, remembered: the tree taller than the house. This crab bigger than the boat.

image.prompt: close-up of a man looking at a child's crayon drawing where the crab is bigger than the boat beside it

panels.composition: Wood, the next day, at the frame shop's counter — as a customer. The OWNER, glasses on a cord. A red frame.

balloons.text: You always said no mat for the kids' ones.
I remember everything, Arthur. It's a small shop.

image.prompt: a thin man as a customer at a frame-shop counter choosing a red frame from an older woman with glasses on a cord
image.notes: 'Arthur' — the owner's third and last use.

panels.composition: The red-framed crab on Gully's corkboard, above the register, beside the twenty-year-old pencil rough. The girl looking up at it.

image.prompt: a child's crab drawing in a red frame pinned to a crowded corkboard above a shop register, a small girl looking up at it, no words

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; Sundays wet-on-wet
art.palette: ink and one tone; Sundays gray-green, fog, rust

notes: Wood as a frame-shop customer. Red, no mat. 'I remember everything, Arthur.'
